what_happened: SEPA Instant reject with AC01: the beneficiary's bank could not use the IBAN, either because its format is invalid or because it does not exist at that bank. No money moved, since the payment was rejected before settlement.
next_step: Platform support resolves this with the customer (FIRST_LINE route). Per the scheme suggestion, the payer should obtain the beneficiary's correct IBAN before any new instruction is created; do not resend the payment with the same IBAN. This is team guidance.
customer_message: Your recent instant transfer was rejected because the account number (IBAN) for the recipient could not be used by their bank. No money was taken from your account for this payment. Please check the recipient's IBAN with them and contact us if you need help.

what_happened: AC04 means the beneficiary's account is closed at the beneficiary's bank, usually because the beneficiary closed it after the payer last paid them. The payment was rejected at the REJECT stage, so no money moved. In some SEPA countries the same situation may arrive as MS03 instead, which can also reflect a regulatory reason. Route is FIRST_LINE: platform support resolves it with the customer.
next_step: Platform support should contact the customer to explain that the beneficiary's account is closed and that the payer needs to obtain the beneficiary's new account details directly from the beneficiary before any new payment is made. Do not resend the payment to the original account.
customer_message: Your payment was not sent because the account it was addressed to is closed at the recipient's bank. No money has left your account. To proceed, please contact the person or business you were paying to and ask for their current account details, then let us know so we can help you with the next step.

what_happened: AC06 means the beneficiary's bank has blocked the beneficiary's account for transactions, so the SEPA Instant payment was rejected before settlement and no money moved. The block may be due to a court order or a block placed by the beneficiary's bank itself, such as for suspected misuse or at the beneficiary's request.
next_step: Route to Platform support (first line) to resolve with the customer. Suggested approach from the scheme rule: the customer contacts the beneficiary to agree an alternative account or another way to pay.
customer_message: Your instant transfer was not completed because the recipient's account is currently blocked by their bank, so no money was taken from your account. You may wish to contact the recipient to agree an alternative account or another way to pay.

what_happened: AG01 means the SEPA Instant payment was rejected before settlement because this type of transaction is not allowed on the account, usually because the beneficiary's details point to an account that cannot receive SCT Inst. No money moved. Our bank is the payer's bank.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. Per the scheme rule, the customer should agree with the beneficiary on another payment method; a standard (non-instant) SEPA credit transfer re-initiated by our bank is possible only if the customer and bank agreed this beforehand and applicable law allows it.
customer_message: Your instant payment was not completed because this type of transaction is not allowed on the account involved. No money has left your account. You may wish to contact the beneficiary to agree on another way to send the payment.

what_happened: AM05 means the clearing system or the beneficiary's bank treated this SEPA Instant payment as a duplicate of an identical payment sent or processed very recently, so it was stopped before settlement and no money moved. The EPC names a technical or human error at the originator or originator's bank as the typical root cause, and our route for this case is DEVELOPER (technical or system issue).
next_step: Check whether the payment was really duplicated by comparing it with recent identical payments from this customer, and look for a technical or system fault on our side that could have resent it. The EPC suggests the originator and its bank verify this. Routing is DEVELOPER per the routing table.
customer_message: Your recent instant transfer was not completed because our systems flagged it as a possible duplicate of a recent payment. No money has left your account. We are checking the payment and will contact you if we need anything from you.

what_happened: AB05 means the beneficiary's bank did not receive or process this SEPA Instant payment within the scheme time limit. The payment was rejected before settlement, so no money moved. The cause may lie anywhere between our bank, the clearing system and the beneficiary's bank.
next_step: Platform support should resolve this with the customer (FIRST_LINE route). Confirm with the customer that no funds were debited, then discuss options: re-issuing the instant payment later, using a standard SEPA credit transfer instead, or the customer contacting the beneficiary for another payment method.
customer_message: Your instant payment to the beneficiary was not completed because it did not reach the beneficiary's bank within the required time limit. No money has left your account for this payment. You can try sending the payment again later, use a standard SEPA credit transfer instead, or contact the beneficiary to agree another way to pay.

what_happened: MS02 means the beneficiary refused the payment when it was presented, on the beneficiary's own instruction not to accept funds from this account, originator, or scheme, and gave no reason. The reject happened before settlement, so no money moved. The reason is withheld on purpose and should not be inferred.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. Per the EPC suggestion in KB-SCTI-MS02-01, the customer may contact the beneficiary directly to agree how to settle any amount owed. Do not attempt to retry or guess the cause.
customer_message: Your payment was not completed because the recipient's bank declined it and gave no reason. No funds were moved. If you need to settle a matter with the recipient, you can contact them directly. Our support team can help you with next steps.

what_happened: MS03 means the beneficiary's bank rejected the payment without a specific reason. The EPC allows this code only where national law forbids more precise codes, so the cause could be a closed account or a regulatory reason. No money moved, and the other bank gave no reason on purpose.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. Per the EPC scheme rule, the customer should contact the beneficiary directly to agree how to settle the obligation. Do not try to infer the underlying cause from the code.
customer_message: Your payment was rejected by the beneficiary's bank, and no reason was given. No money has left your account. You may wish to contact the beneficiary directly to agree how to settle the payment.

what_happened: RR04 means the beneficiary's bank stopped this SEPA Instant payment at reject stage for a regulatory reason, typically a possible AML, sanctions or counter-terrorist-financing hit. No funds moved. The route is COMPLIANCE, so the compliance team should review the stop.
next_step: Hand to Compliance. Do not contact the customer about the reason; Compliance decides what, if anything, is said.

what_happened: AC01 on a SEPA Direct Debit return means the debtor's IBAN was invalid in format or does not exist at the debtor's bank. The money settled and came back, so this is a return after settlement, and the root cause may be the debtor's data, the creditor's own IBAN records, or a technical issue on collection creation.
next_step: Route to Platform support for first-line resolution with the customer, as the routing table specifies. Ask the customer to contact the debtor to obtain the correct IBAN, and check the data the debtor provided if the mandate was amended. This is scheme guidance, not team guidance.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected was returned because the payer's account number (IBAN) was not valid or could not be found. Please contact the payer to confirm their correct IBAN. Our support team can help you with next steps.

what_happened: AC04 means the debtor's account was closed at the debtor's bank, usually after the creditor's last collection from it. Here the payment settled and was then returned, so funds were moved back. The route is FIRST_LINE, so platform support resolves it with the customer.
next_step: Platform support should contact the customer, who is the creditor, to ask them to obtain the debtor's new account details from the debtor, as the EPC suggests. Note that some SEPA countries send MS03 instead of AC04 for this situation, so check the code before relying on the AC04 explanation.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected was returned by the payer's bank because the payer's account is closed. To continue collecting, please contact the payer to ask for their current account details.

what_happened: AC06 means the debtor's account, or this specific collection, is blocked. The direct debit was returned after settlement, so funds moved and came back. Route is FIRST_LINE: platform support resolves it with the customer. The EPC describes blocks from a court order or from the debtor's bank (e.g., suspected misuse or debtor request).
next_step: Platform support should contact the customer to agree an alternative account or another way to pay, as suggested by the scheme guidance. The bank can act on the creditor's behalf only if that has been agreed. Confirm with the customer which block type applies before proceeding; the scheme passage does not say how to tell them apart.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected was returned because the payer's account is blocked for this payment. We can help you agree another way to get paid. Please get in touch so we can discuss an alternative account or payment method.

what_happened: AG01 means the direct debit was forbidden on the debtor's account for regulatory reasons, typically because the debtor supplied details of a type of account (such as savings) from which direct debits cannot be booked. The payment was returned after settlement, so funds moved and came back. Per the scheme rule, AG01 must not be used for a SDD B2B collection presented to a consumer account; that case should carry AC13 instead.
next_step: Platform support resolves this with the customer under the FIRST_LINE route. Per the scheme guidance, the creditor should contact the debtor to agree on another payment account or payment instrument. Also check whether the collection was a B2B collection presented to a consumer account, since that would indicate AC13 rather than AG01.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected from your payer was returned because the account it was drawn from cannot accept direct debits. Please contact your payer to agree on another payment account or payment method, and our support team can help you with next steps.

what_happened: AM04 means the debtor's account did not hold enough money to cover this SEPA Direct Debit, and the payment was returned after settlement, so funds moved and came back. The EPC also names a creditor-side cause: missing or late pre-notification of the collection date and amount.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. The scheme suggests the creditor contact the debtor so they can make funds available, and checking whether pre-notification was sent and on time. This is the scheme's suggested action, not a decision, and the operations agent should confirm it.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected was returned because the payer's account did not have enough funds to cover it. You may wish to contact the payer so they can make funds available, and check that the payer was notified of the collection date and amount in advance.

what_happened: AM05 (duplication) on this SEPA Direct Debit means the clearing system or the debtor's bank treated the collection as a duplicate of an identical one sent very recently. The return came after settlement, so funds moved and were sent back. The EPC names a technical or human error at the creditor or creditor's bank as the root cause, and the route is DEVELOPER (technical or system issue).
next_step: Check whether the collection was actually duplicated, looking for an identical collection sent or processed very recently, as the scheme suggests. Route to the developer team for a technical or system review. Note that this route is the bank's routing table, and any further steps should follow team guidance and the rulebook where applicable.
customer_message: Your direct debit collection was returned by the payer's bank because it was flagged as a possible duplicate of a recent collection. We are looking into whether the collection was sent more than once and will contact you with an update.

what_happened: MD01 means the debtor's bank found no valid mandate for this SEPA Direct Debit, or the debtor claimed an unauthorised collection. The code alone does not show which of the listed situations applies (no mandate, unconfirmed B2B mandate, failed B2B mandate retrieval, bank cancellation after 36 months unused, or an SDD Core unauthorised refund request), so the collection details need checking. The payment was returned after settlement, so the funds have moved back.
next_step: Platform support should resolve this with the creditor: check the collection's mandate reference against the mandate information, confirm whether the mandate exists and is active, and establish whether this is a B2B or Core collection. If the debtor requested a refund, contact the debtor as the scheme suggests. This is first-line routing, so keep the handling with platform support.
customer_message: A direct debit we collected was returned with reason MD01, which means the payer's bank could not find a valid mandate for it. Please check your mandate details and the mandate reference used on this collection, and contact our platform support team so we can review it with you.

what_happened: MD06 means the debtor (payer) used their unconditional right to a refund of an authorised SDD Core collection, which can be claimed until 8 weeks after the debit date. The refund came back after settlement, so the creditor (our customer) has lost the funds, and it can arrive weeks after a collection looked successful.
next_step: Route is FIRST_LINE: platform support resolves it with the customer. Per the scheme guidance, the suggested creditor action is to contact the debtor; confirm whether the pre-notified amount matched the amount collected, since that mismatch is one possible trigger. Team guidance is not supplied for this case, so the operations agent should decide the follow-up.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected was refunded to the payer after it had settled. We are looking into the details with you and will explain the options available to you.

what_happened: MS02 means the debtor (payer) refused this SEPA Direct Debit collection after it was presented, for example after receiving the pre-notification, and gave no reason. The decision came from the debtor, not from the debtor's bank, and the money moved and was returned after settlement.
next_step: Platform support resolves this with the customer (FIRST_LINE route). The scheme suggests the creditor contact the debtor; the bank gave no reason, so do not speculate about causes with the customer.
customer_message: A direct debit you collected was returned. The payer refused the payment and no reason was given. Please contact the payer directly if you would like to follow up, or reach out to our support team if you have questions about this payment.

what_happened: MS03 means the debtor's bank returned the direct debit after settlement without a specific reason, because national privacy law forbids the precise code. The underlying cause could be a closed account, insufficient funds, a deceased debtor or a regulatory reason, and the reason is withheld on purpose.
next_step: Platform support should contact the customer (the creditor) to resolve this first-line. The scheme's suggested action is for the creditor to contact the debtor to find the cause. This is team guidance from the knowledge base, and a person decides the action.
customer_message: Your direct debit payment was returned by the payer's bank. No reason was given. Please contact our support team so we can help you decide on next steps.

what_happened: RR04 means the debtor's bank stopped this SEPA Direct Debit for a regulatory reason (possible AML, sanctions or counter-terrorist-financing hit). The money moved and was returned after settlement, and we are the creditor's bank. Route is COMPLIANCE, so the compliance team owns this case.
next_step: Hand to Compliance. Do not contact the customer about the reason; Compliance decides what, if anything, is said.

what_happened: AC03 means the creditor (recipient) account number is invalid or missing, per the ISO 20022 definition. This is an RTP reject before settlement, so no money moved. The route is FIRST_LINE, so platform support resolves it with the customer.
next_step: Team guidance (not a scheme rule): have the customer confirm the recipient's account number directly with the recipient before sending a new payment, and do not resubmit with the same details. If several AC03 rejections hit the same saved payee, check whether the customer's saved payee details are wrong.
customer_message: Your payment to the recipient was not completed because the recipient's account number could not be verified. No money was taken from your account. Please confirm the recipient's account number directly with them before sending a new payment.

what_happened: AC04 means the recipient's account number has been closed at the bank holding it, so RTP rejected the payment before settlement and no money moved. The route is FIRST_LINE, handled by platform support with the customer.
next_step: Team guidance, not a scheme rule: have platform support work with the customer to obtain current account details from the recipient. Do not retry the payment to the same account, and do not suggest the recipient's bank made an error.
customer_message: Your real-time payment was not completed because the recipient's account has been closed. No money was taken from your account. Please contact the recipient to get their current account details, then start a new payment with those details.

what_happened: AC06 means the receiving party's account is blocked for transactions, so the RTP payment was rejected before settlement and no funds moved. The block is on the other party's account, not on our customer's account.
next_step: Team guidance (KB-RTP-AC06-01): this is a first-line case, so Platform support should work with the customer. Do not guess or request the reason for the block; that decision belongs to the recipient's bank.
customer_message: Your payment was not completed because the recipient's account cannot accept payments right now. No money was taken from your account for this payment. You may want to agree another account or payment method with the recipient.

what_happened: AG01 on this RTP payment means the transaction is forbidden on this type of account, per the ISO 20022 definition. The payment was rejected before settlement, so no money moved. The routing table sends this case to the developer team.
next_step: Per team guidance (not a scheme rule), the developer team should first check whether anything on our side, such as configuration or message content, caused the rejection. If nothing is wrong on our side, first line can ask the customer to agree another payment method with the recipient.
customer_message: Your real-time payment to the recipient was not completed because this type of transaction is not permitted on the account. No money was taken from your account. We are looking into the details, and we will contact you if we need anything further from you.

what_happened: RTP reason code AM04 (Insufficient Funds) means the funds available were not enough to cover the payment amount. This payment was rejected before settlement, so no money moved. The route is Treasury, which handles bank liquidity or prefunded balance issues, so the first question is our own RTP funding position rather than the customer's balance.
next_step: Route to Treasury to check our bank's RTP funding position before anyone contacts the customer. This is team guidance (KB-RTP-AM04-01), not a scheme rule. Do not tell the customer they lack funds unless Treasury confirms the cause was on the customer's side.
customer_message: We were unable to complete your payment of this RTP transfer, and no money has left your account. We are looking into the reason and will update you once we have more information. Please contact us if you have questions.

what_happened: DS24 on this RTP reject means the waiting time expired because the order was incomplete, so the payment timed out before completing. The payment was rejected before settlement and no money moved. The routing table sends this case to the developer team (technical or system issue).
next_step: Team guidance, not a scheme rule: confirm the original payment's final status with a pacs.028 status request before anyone resends, to avoid a duplicate payment. The developer team should check our connection and processing logs for this payment.
customer_message: Your payment did not complete. Please don't send it again until we've confirmed its status.

what_happened: RR04 means the receiving bank stopped this RTP payment for a regulatory reason, such as a possible AML, sanctions or counter-terrorist-financing hit. The payment was rejected before settlement, so no funds moved. Route is COMPLIANCE, so this is for the compliance team to review.
next_step: Hand to Compliance. Do not contact the customer about the reason; Compliance decides what, if anything, is said.

what_happened: The payment was flagged as possibly fraudulent.
next_step: Pass to the fraud team immediately. Do not retry, refund or contact the other party until the fraud team decides.
customer_message: We are reviewing this payment. Please contact us if you have any questions.
note: No guidance available: showing the baseline for this code (D7).

what_happened: Reason code CNOR is not in our code table.
next_step: Escalate for manual triage; no explanation is available for this code.

what_happened: No failure to explain: the payment was accepted or settled.
No failure to explain yet: the payment is still pending. Do not resend; wait for the final status or request it (pacs.028 status request).
The other bank rejected or returned the payment because the other party's account is blocked.
next_step: Tell the customer the other party's account cannot receive or pay this transaction, and suggest they agree another account or payment method with the other party. Do not speculate about why it is blocked.
customer_message: Your payment could not be completed because the other party's account cannot accept it. Please contact them to agree another way to pay.
note: No guidance available: showing the baseline for this code (D7).

what_happened: AC04 means the beneficiary's account is closed at the beneficiary's bank, so the instant payment was rejected before settlement and no money moved. It typically happens because the beneficiary closed the account after the customer last paid them.
next_step: Route to Platform support (FIRST_LINE) to resolve with the customer. Per the scheme rule, the customer should contact the beneficiary to obtain their new account details. Note that some SEPA countries send MS03 instead of AC04 for the same situation, so check the code and country before concluding.
customer_message: Your recent instant transfer could not be completed because the beneficiary's account is closed at their bank. No money has left your account. Please contact the beneficiary to get their current account details, then send the payment again.
